newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Ukraine beet forecast to produce 3 mln T whites.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine beet forecast to produce 3 mln T whites.

text.p: The head of a Ukrainian government analytical centre forecast said on Wednesday that Ukraine would produce three million tonnes of white sugar from domestic beets in the 1996 crop year, down from nearly 3.5 million tonnes in 1995.

Oleg Tymkiv, chief of the agricultural section of the Trade Ministry's information-analysis centre for monitoring of foreign trade, said Ukraine would export 1.5 million tonnes of whites from Ukrainian beets over September 1996 to September 1997.
Ukrainian whites exports, from domestic beets, were 1.9 million tonnes, including 1.6 million tonnes to Russia, in the 1995 crop year, he said.
Ukraine also produces and exports white sugar from imported raws. The centre did not include that output in its forecast.
Tymkiv said the Ukrainian beet crop would produce about three tonnes of sugar per harvested hectare, or 0.4-0.5 tonnes less than last year.
Beet losses would be higher in 1996 than in 1995, when 91 percent of sown land was harvested.
Only 75 percent of the 1.3 million hectares sown to beets in Ukraine this year were healthy as of mid-summer, he said, though he declined to forecast what percentage would be brought in.

Tymkiv said rainy weather had slowed the early harvest and some farmers would probably be forced to leave beets in the ground when winter set in, though harvesting is currently proceeding well in good, sunny weather.
Sugar refineries are also having power problems due to a lack of mazut heavy fuel, he said.
Ukrainian Agriculture Minister Anatoly Khorishko earlier on Wednesday predicted that Ukraine's refined sugar output from its 26-million-tonne 1996 beet crop would be 3.2 million tonnes.
